nodes.title: Abelian Varieties
nodes.description: complex tori, polarizations, theta functions, isogenies, the dual abelian variety, and abelian varieties over general fields. Two Parts: (I) complex-analytic, complex tori, the Appell–Humbert theorem, the Riemann relations, theta functions, the dual torus and isogenies, endomorphism algebras and CM; (II) algebraic over arbitrary fields (full scheme-theoretic), rigidity, the theorem of the cube, Tate modules, the dual abelian variety and the Weil pairing, the Rosati involution and Albert's classification, Jacobians, and abelian varieties over finite fields (Frobenius, Weil conjectures, Honda–Tate). Prereqs Algebraic Geometry, Complex Analysis, Commutative Algebra, Homological Algebra; strongly recommended Elliptic Curves (the g=1 model). Keystone of the arithmetic-geometry tower, between Elliptic Curves and Shimura Varieties.

nodes.title: Algebra
nodes.description: The Algebra mega-book, the single compiled volume threading core algebra, commutative algebra, classical algebraic geometry, algebraic number theory, representation theory, homological algebra, and category theory.

nodes.title: Algebraic Geometry
nodes.description: **megabook**; one physical source (EYNTKA_algGeo.tex) compiling three separately-citable sub-books under a container codename. Legacy citeNateAlgGeo remain valid (they cite the scheme-theory material now in Part I); prefer the precise sub-codename going forward. The sub-books

nodes.title: Algebraic K-Theory
nodes.description: projective modules, K_0, K_1 (Whitehead group), K_2 (Steinberg group, Matsumoto's theorem), and Quillen's higher K-theory (BGL^+, Q-construction).

nodes.title: Algebraic Number Theory
nodes.description: rings of integers, ideals, integral bases, norms, traces, splitting of primes, ideal class group, Dirichlet's unit theorem, Kronecker-Weber theorem.

nodes.title: Algebraic Topology
nodes.description: fundamental group, covering spaces, singular homology, CW complexes, cohomology rings, Poincaré duality.

nodes.title: Calculus
nodes.description: Multivariable calculus done carefully, vector fields, paths, line/surface integrals, the inverse and implicit function theorems, and Stokes' theorem in 2–3 dimensions. The computational/geometric bridge from elementary analysis to differential geometry.

nodes.title: Category Theory
nodes.description: the working categorical language (strict 1-category theory), in eight chapters: categories/functors/natural transformations, the Yoneda lemma and representability, universal properties with limits and colimits, adjunctions (including the adjoint functor theorems), monads and their algebras, **Kan extensions** as the core-theory capstone ("all concepts are Kan extensions"), then a structured-categories coda, **monoidal categories** (Mac Lane coherence, symmetric/closed) and **enriched and (strict) 2-categories**, that ends by pointing across the coherence seam to the weak/homotopical sequel Higher Category Theory. Standing cast of example categories in place of one running example; arc credited to Riehl's *Category Theory in Context*. **Abelian categories are deliberately ceded to Homological Algebra**. A subfiles sub-book compiled into the *Algebra* mega-book (the "Category Theory" Part) that also compiles standalone with the full EYNTKA skeleton, guarded via ifstandalonesubfile.

nodes.title: Class Field Theory
nodes.description: local fields, places, ray class groups, idele group, Hasse principle.

nodes.title: Classical Algebraic Geometry
nodes.description: algebraic sets, varieties, normalization, dimension, blow-ups.

nodes.title: Commutative Algebra
nodes.description: integral extensions, localization, completion, Hilbert's basis theorem.

nodes.title: Complex Analysis
nodes.description: Cauchy–Riemann, analytic continuation, residue theorem, elliptic functions, Riemann surfaces.

nodes.title: Core Algebra
nodes.description: groups, rings, modules, fields.

nodes.title: Core Probability
nodes.description: the measure-free treatment (measure theory built inline, not assumed): distributions, expected value, variance, law of large numbers, Erdős-Rényi graphs, exponential/concentration inequalities, Gaussian distribution, finite Markov chains. The accessible entry point; the measure-theoretic flagship is *Probability*.

nodes.title: Core Representation Theory
nodes.description: Maschke's theorem, Schur's lemma, Wedderburn-Artin theorem, character theory, induced representations, Frobenius reciprocity, quiver theory.

nodes.title: C*-Algebras and K-Theory
nodes.description: C*-algebras, Gelfand–Naimark duality, states and the GNS construction, representations, and the K-theory of C*-algebras (K_0/K_1, six-term exact sequence, Bott, the Toeplitz index map).

nodes.title: Differential Geometry
nodes.description: smooth manifolds, de Rham cohomology, connections.

nodes.title: Elementary Analysis
nodes.description: real numbers, sequences, series, calculus basics.

nodes.title: Elliptic Curves
nodes.description: Weierstrass equations, group law, isogenies, Weil pairing, Mordell–Weil theorem, Hasse's theorem, Galois representations, CM theory, modular forms, modularity, BSD conjecture.

nodes.title: Étale Cohomology
nodes.description: the étale site and étale cohomology of schemes. Four Parts (14 chapters): (I) *the étale topology*, étale morphisms and Henselian local rings, the étale fundamental group pi_1^ét (finite étale covers, Galois categories, Riemann existence, owned here, the series' home of the topic), the étale site and its sheaves; (II) *étale cohomology*, cohomology and the cohomology of a point (= Galois cohomology), Kummer/Artin–Schreier/G_m, the cohomology of curves, constructible sheaves and finiteness; (III) *the Brauer group and the fundamental theorems*, the cohomological Brauer group Br(X)=H^2_ét(X,G_m) (Azumaya, **Gabber proved**), base change / Künneth / comparison, purity / cycle class / Poincaré duality; (IV) *ell-adic cohomology and the Weil conjectures*, ell-adic sheaves, the Lefschetz trace formula + rationality + functional equation, Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles, and **Deligne's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis in full** (Weil I). The series' bridge from scheme theory to arithmetic geometry, the upstream home of the geometric Brauer group, and the home of the étale fundamental group. Prereqs Modern Algebraic Geometry, Commutative Algebra, Homological Algebra, Group and Galois Cohomology; **co-requisite Moduli, Deformation Theory, and Stacks** (cites its descent/sites + gerbe interpretation of H^2; supplies back the Gabber proof + higher-dimensional Brauer computations that book defers). Feeds Moduli, Deformation Theory, and Stacks, Hodge Theory (cycle class map / comparison), Abelian Varieties.

nodes.title: Functional Analysis
nodes.description: Banach spaces, Hilbert spaces, Hahn–Banach theorem, open mapping theorem, spectral theory of bounded operators.

nodes.title: Group and Galois Cohomology
nodes.description: the series' cohomological source-book, in three arcs: **group cohomology** (discrete + finite: derived functors, the bar resolution, low-degree interpretations and extensions, homology and coinvariants, Tate cohomology and cup products), **structure theory** (cohomological dimension, pro-p groups and Golod–Shafarevich, the Brauer group), and **Galois cohomology of fields** (the profinite refinement, local and global Tate duality, the Poitou–Tate sequence, class formations and reciprocity, descent and non-abelian cohomology, Selmer/Ш). Feeds Class Field Theory, Elliptic Curves, Local Langlands for GL₂(F), Moduli, Deformation Theory, and Stacks, Étale Cohomology.

nodes.title: Geometric Analysis
nodes.description: Ricci flow, minimal surfaces, spectral geometry, variational methods. Named explicitly in Riemannian Geometry Ch. 14 as a projected companion volume.

nodes.title: Algebraic Groups and Representations
nodes.description: linear algebraic groups, root systems, Dynkin classification, highest-weight theory, Weyl character formula, Borel–Weil–Bott.

nodes.title: General Relativity
nodes.description: Pseudo-Riemannian geometry, the Einstein equations, causality, singularity theorems. Named explicitly in Riemannian Geometry Ch. 14 as a projected companion volume.

nodes.title: Harmonic Analysis
nodes.description: Fourier transform, convolution, distribution theory, Sobolev spaces, topological groups, Haar measure, Pontryagin duality.

nodes.title: Higher Category Theory
nodes.description: The weak / homotopy-coherent / higher-dimensional sequel to Category Theory: simplicial sets and nerves, model categories (Quillen), quasi-categories / ∞-categories (Lurie–Riehl), homotopy (co)limits, stable ∞-categories and the bridge to derived/triangulated categories, and a survey of ∞-toposes.

nodes.title: Hodge Theory
nodes.description: compact Kähler geometry, Hodge decomposition, polarized Hodge structures, Lefschetz theorems, variations of Hodge structure, period maps and Mumford–Tate domains, mixed Hodge structures, algebraic cycles.

nodes.title: Homological Algebra
nodes.description: abelian/triangulated categories, derived functors, spectral sequences.

nodes.title: Intersection Theory
nodes.description: *Intersection Theory*, algebraic cycles, rational equivalence and Chow groups, proper pushforward / flat pullback, Chern classes via Segre classes and the splitting principle, deformation to the normal cone, the intersection product and the Chow ring A*(X), cycle class maps and adequate equivalence relations, Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch, and enumerative geometry (Grassmannian Chow ring, Schubert calculus, degeneracy loci). Spine: Fulton, adapted; prereqs cited to Part I.

nodes.title: Vector Bundles and K-Theory
nodes.description: vector bundles, classifying spaces BO/BU, topological K^0/K^1, Bott periodicity, and characteristic classes (Stiefel–Whitney, Chern, Euler, Pontryagin). Purely topological.

nodes.title: Local Langlands for GL₂(F)
nodes.description: smooth representations of locally profinite groups, Hecke algebras, principal series, supercuspidal representations, local L-functions, epsilon-factors, Weil groups, Deligne representations.

nodes.title: Lie Groups
nodes.description: the analytic / differential-geometric half of Lie theory, complementary to the algebraic-groups treatment in Algebraic Groups and Representations. Four Parts: (I) Lie groups and their Lie algebras, matrix groups and the classical groups, the exponential map, left-invariant vector fields, the closed-subgroup theorem, the Lie group–Lie algebra correspondence, BCH, homogeneous spaces and covering groups; (II) structure of Lie algebras, solvable/nilpotent (Engel, Lie), the Cartan criteria, Weyl complete reducibility, Levi, the root space decomposition, root systems, and the Cartan–Killing classification; (III) compact Lie groups and their representations, invariant integration, the Peter–Weyl theorem, maximal tori and the Weyl integration formula, the Weyl character and dimension formulas; (IV) real forms and symmetric spaces, complexification, the Cartan decomposition, the Iwasawa decomposition KAN, and Riemannian symmetric spaces bridging to Riemannian Geometry. Running example SU(2). Prereqs Differential Geometry, Core Algebra, Core Representation Theory, Topology, Real Analysis/Functional Analysis; cites Harmonic Analysis for Haar measure.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra
nodes.description: The concrete / computational first-and-second course in linear algebra over R and C: linear systems and Gaussian elimination, matrices and determinants, vector spaces and linear maps concretely, eigenvalues and diagonalization, inner-product spaces, and symmetric/Hermitian forms. The pedagogical on-ramp to the abstract, module-theoretic treatment Core Algebra develops from scratch (Ch 14-16, spectral theorem included); recommended background for the abstract-algebra and Lie/representation-theory tracks, a hard prerequisite of neither.

nodes.title: Linear Elliptic and Parabolic Equations
nodes.description: the graduate linear-PDE spine: weak formulations and Lax–Milgram, existence by variational methods, the two regularity theories (Schauder and L^p), maximum principles, Green's functions, spectral theory of elliptic operators, and the heat equation with semigroups; elliptic systems on domains. Cites the analysis foundations for Sobolev/distributions/singular integrals (does not re-derive them). Prereqs Functional Analysis, Measure Theory, Harmonic Analysis, Calculus.

nodes.title: Logic
nodes.description: first-order language, propositional language, soundness, completeness, compactness, computability, Turing machines, Gödel's incompleteness theorem.

nodes.title: Measure Theory
nodes.description: sigma-algebras, outer measure, Borel/Lebesgue measures, product measure, signed and complex measures, Lebesgue-Radon-Nikodym theorem.

nodes.title: Modern Algebraic Geometry
nodes.description: *Modern Algebraic Geometry*, scheme theory, sheaves of modules, sheaf cohomology, curves and surfaces. Essentially complete (Part I ch. 1–5 are source-book voice anchors).

nodes.title: Moduli, Deformation Theory, and Stacks
nodes.description: Moduli theory in three movements: functor-of-points representability and the construction toolkit (Hilbert/Quot schemes, geometric invariant theory); deformation theory (first-order deformations as cohomology, obstructions, the naive cotangent complex, Schlessinger's criteria); and the stacks that represent moduli problems with automorphisms (descent and sites, fibered categories, algebraic/Deligne-Mumford/Artin stacks, Artin's representability criteria, gerbes and the Brauer group). Closes with an application to the moduli of curves. Spun out from the Algebraic Geometry mega-book's Part III.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Wave and Dispersive Equations
nodes.description: linear wave (d'Alembert, energy method) as the foundation, then nonlinear wave equations (Klainerman–Sobolev, null conditions, global existence) and dispersive methods (Littlewood–Paley, Strichartz). The analytic engine of general relativity (the Einstein equations are a nonlinear wave system). The linear elliptic/parabolic core moved to Linear Elliptic and Parabolic Equations. Prereqs Functional Analysis, Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE), Calculus, Harmonic Analysis.

nodes.title: Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
nodes.description: Picard-Lindelöf theorem, linear systems, matrix exponentials, Lyapunov stability, boundary value problems, Sturm-Liouville theory, Green's functions.

nodes.title: Preliminaries
nodes.description: series-wide foundation: logic, naive set theory, proof techniques, relations and orders, functions, cardinality, elementary number theory, first exposure to categories.

nodes.title: Probability
nodes.description: The measure-theoretic flagship (prereq measure theory): probability spaces as measure spaces, random variables and independence, modes of convergence, laws of large numbers, characteristic functions and the central limit theorem, conditional expectation via Radon–Nikodym, and discrete-time martingales. Ends before continuous-time processes.

nodes.title: Real Analysis
nodes.description: The Analysis mega-book, the compiled real-analysis volume threading measure theory, functional analysis, and harmonic analysis.

nodes.title: Is $(\mathbb{R},+)$ an Automorphism Group?
nodes.description: a leaf research monograph compiling a reduction theory for the question "does there exist a group G with Aut(G)cong(R,+)?" (open). Reduces any witness to an infinite class-2 Miller group with a faithful odd-prime Prüfer action of unbounded cyclotomic level, kills every single-tower and multi-prime configuration, and reduces the sole survivor (the repeated-tower S1 sector) to a module-theoretic burial question. Three Parts: (I) *The Reduction*, abelian/locally-cyclic kills, the class-2 reduction, the Miller-group reframing; (II) *The Prüfer Regime*, the trichotomy collapse to a single cyclotomic regime, target-agnosticism, the torsion program, the odd-prime theorem via the [u]-idempotent and the Amoroso–Dvornicich height bound; (III) *The Survivor Map and the S1 Frontier*, the shear catastrophe and bigstar-theorems, the q-adic normal form, and the reduction to the burial lemma (WDL), closing with the realization target and open problems. Full-research-narrative posture (failed attempts and repairs are marked-and-included). Prereqs Core Algebra, Homological Algebra, Algebraic Number Theory; soft-cites Group and Galois Cohomology, Commutative Algebra. Compiles the Research-OS project IsRealAutRepble (D1–D60).

nodes.title: Riemannian Geometry
nodes.description: a two-Part backbone. Part I (metric Riemannian geometry): metrics of arbitrary signature, the Levi-Civita connection, geodesics and the exponential map, the curvature tensor, Jacobi fields, comparison theorems (Hopf–Rinow, Bonnet–Myers, Cartan–Hadamard, Rauch), submanifold geometry, curvature and topology, homogeneous and symmetric spaces. Part II (analysis and curvature on manifolds): connections and curvature on vector bundles, Chern–Weil theory, the Hodge–de Rham theorem, the Bochner technique. Pseudo-Riemannian threaded throughout for downstream GR. Prereqs Differential Geometry, Real Analysis, Nonlinear Wave and Dispersive Equations. Part II is a pre-cut split seam. Feeds Hodge Theory (which imports Part II), geometric analysis, GR, and spin/index theory.

nodes.title: Shimura Varieties
nodes.description: the arithmetic-geometry capstone above Abelian Varieties and the geometric gateway to the Langlands program, following Deligne's axiomatic Hodge-theoretic route (Milne/Deligne). Four Parts, twelve chapters: (I) *from modular curves to symmetric domains*, the modular curve as prototype, Hermitian symmetric domains and their three faces, and Hodge structures as representations of the Deligne torus S=Res_C/RG_m; (II) *Shimura data and Shimura varieties*, the axioms SV1-SV3 on a pair (G,X), the reflex field, the double-coset variety G(Q)backslash Xtimes G(A_f)/K with its component structure and Hecke action, and Baily-Borel algebraicity; (III) *canonical models and PEL moduli*, CM/special points and the reciprocity law, existence and uniqueness of canonical models over the reflex field, the Siegel variety A_g and PEL-type moduli of abelian varieties; (IV) *toward automorphic forms and Langlands*, automorphic vector bundles and forms, and the cohomology of Shimura varieties carrying Galois representations (Eichler-Shimura prototype, Langlands-Kottwitz survey). Running examples: the modular curve (GL_2) and the Siegel variety (GSp_2g). Prereqs Abelian Varieties (CM, Albert, Tate modules), Elliptic Curves, Algebraic Groups and Representations, Class Field Theory; coreq Hodge Theory (Mumford-Tate/period domains). The legacy Serre-preliminaries stub (central simple algebras / Brauer group) was archived at bootstrap and cited out to Group and Galois Cohomology/Core Algebra.

nodes.title: Mathematical Statistics
nodes.description: Mathematical statistics on a measure-theoretic-probability base (prereq Probability): statistical models and the decision-theoretic frame, sufficiency and exponential families, point estimation (Cramér–Rao, UMVU, MLE, Bayes), hypothesis testing and confidence sets (Neyman–Pearson, likelihood ratio, duality), large-sample theory (consistency, asymptotic normality, Wilks), and the Gaussian linear model. The statistics/ML arm of the probability tower.

nodes.title: Topology
nodes.description: separation axioms, product/quotient topology, metric spaces, connectedness, compactness, Urysohn lemma, fundamental group, topological groups.

nodes.title: Toric Geometry
nodes.description: the combinatoricsleftrightarrowgeometry dictionary: tori and character lattices; affine toric varieties (the four constructions and their equivalence); rational polyhedral cones, Gordan's lemma, and normal affine toric varieties; projective toric varieties and lattice polytopes; fans and abstract toric varieties; completeness, properness, and toric morphisms; the orbit–cone correspondence; toric Weil/Cartier divisors and the class group; the Cox homogeneous-coordinate construction (toric varieties as torus quotients); ample/nef cones and line bundles; sheaf cohomology of toric varieties and toric Riemann–Roch (lattice-point counting); toric resolution of singularities; capstone on reflexive polytopes, Fano toric varieties, and Batyrev mirror symmetry. **Two-register bridge:** the combinatorial spine (Parts I–IV) is developed over k=bar k (default C) and requires only *Classical Algebraic Geometry* + *Commutative Algebra*; scheme-theoretic material is threaded as marked "Scheme upgrade" asides, and the cohomology Part escalates to *Algebraic Geometry* as a recommended co-requisite. The book is thus both a gateway example-bed reachable before schemes and a payoff of scheme theory, the series' canonical toric example-bed.

clusters.label: Langlands programme
clusters.description: Toward the local Langlands correspondence for GL₂, representation theory and class field theory up through smooth representations and the GL₂ case.

clusters.label: Arithmetic geometry
clusters.description: The arithmetic of varieties, elliptic curves, abelian varieties, and Shimura varieties over number fields, resting on algebraic and arithmetic foundations.

clusters.label: Hodge theory & cycles
clusters.description: Complex and Kähler geometry toward Hodge theory, algebraic cycles, and the (integral) Hodge conjecture.

clusters.label: K-theory
clusters.description: The three flavours of K-theory, topological, algebraic, and operator (C*), and their shared homotopical/homological foundations.

clusters.label: Analysis → PDE
clusters.description: The analysis ladder, from elementary analysis through measure theory and functional analysis to ODE and PDE.
